title: Cain to the Flood, part 1 of 5: Cain and Abel; the generations of Adam
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The earliest ages of the world, long before the flood: wild open country, people dressed in simple garments of animal skin or rough undyed wool, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

ADAM_SKIN.name: Adam
ADAM_SKIN.desc: Adam, the first man, about thirty years old, lean and strong with broad shoulders, warm brown skin, short dark curly hair, a short dark beard, dark eyes and an open, thoughtful face, wearing a simple sleeveless knee-length garment of tawny brown animal skin that covers his chest and is tied at the waist with a strip of hide, barefoot

EVE_SKIN.name: Eve
EVE_SKIN.desc: Eve, the first woman, in her early twenties, warm brown skin, very long wavy black-brown hair falling to her waist, large dark eyes, full brows and a gentle open face, wearing a simple garment of tawny brown animal skin that covers her from her shoulders to her calves, tied at the waist with a strip of hide, barefoot

CAIN.name: Cain
CAIN.desc: Cain, the firstborn son of Adam, a powerfully built man in his late twenties with warm brown skin, thick black shoulder-length hair, a short black beard, heavy dark brows and deep-set dark eyes, wearing a sleeveless knee-length garment of dark brown animal skin tied at the waist with a strip of hide, barefoot

ABEL.name: Abel
ABEL.desc: Abel, the younger son of Adam, a slender man in his early twenties with warm brown skin, short curly dark-brown hair, a light youthful beard and a gentle open face, wearing a knee-length garment of pale cream sheepskin tied at the waist with a strip of hide, barefoot

LAMECH_C.name: Lamech of the line of Cain
LAMECH_C.desc: Lamech, a descendant of Cain, a tall hard-faced man of about forty with warm brown skin, a shaved head, a thick black beard and a scar across one cheek, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough dark wool with a broad leather belt and a grey wolf pelt over one shoulder

SETH.name: Seth
SETH.desc: Seth, a son of Adam, a man of about thirty who looks very like his father: lean and strong with warm brown skin, short dark curly hair, a short dark beard and dark thoughtful eyes, wearing a knee-length garment of light brown animal skin with a rough undyed wool mantle over one shoulder, barefoot

ENOCH.name: Enoch of the line of Seth
ENOCH.desc: Enoch, a descendant of Seth, a tall spare man who looks about thirty-five, with warm brown skin, long straight black hair tied back, a neat dark beard and calm bright eyes, wearing an ankle-length tunic of rough undyed cream wool with a plain rope belt, barefoot

NOAH.name: Noah
NOAH.desc: Noah, a strong weathered man who looks about fifty, with warm brown skin, thick grey-streaked dark hair to his collar, a full grey-streaked beard, deep-set kind eyes and a lined brow, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough undyed brown wool with a leather belt and a darker wool mantle over one shoulder, and simple leather sandals

segs.text: And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain.
With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man,
she said.
Later she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel.
Now Abel was a keeper of sheep, while Cain was a tiller of the soil.
So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD,
while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock.
And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering,
but He had no regard for Cain and his offering.
So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.
Why are you angry,
said the LORD to Cain,
and why has your countenance fallen?
If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.
Then Cain said to his brother Abel,
Let us go out to the field.
And while they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
And the LORD said to Cain,
Where is your brother Abel?
I do not know!
he answered.
Am I my brother’s keeper?
What have you done?
replied the LORD.
The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.
Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you.
You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.
But Cain said to the LORD,
My punishment is greater than I can bear.
Behold, this day You have driven me from the face of the earth, and from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.
Not so!
replied the LORD.
If anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged sevenfold.
And the LORD placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.
So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
And Cain had relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch.
Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.
Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methusael, and Methusael was the father of Lamech.
And Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.
And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.
And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron.
And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
Then Lamech said to his wives:
Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech.
For I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.
And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth,
saying,
God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.
And to Seth also a son was born, and he called him Enosh.
At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.
This is the book of the generations of Adam.
In the day that God created man, He made him in His own likeness.
Male and female He created them, and He blessed them. And in the day they were created, He called them “man.”
When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image; and he named him Seth.
And after he had become the father of Seth, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.
When Seth was 105 years old, he became the father of Enosh.
And after he had become the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died.
When Enosh was 90 years old, he became the father of Kenan.
And after he had become the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Enosh lived a total of 905 years, and then he died.
When Kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.
And after he had become the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died.
When Mahalalel was 65 years old, he became the father of Jared.
And after he had become the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died.
When Jared was 162 years old, he became the father of Enoch.
And after he had become the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Jared lived a total of 962 years, and then he died.
When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah.
And after he had become the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Enoch lived a total of 365 years.
Enoch walked with God,
and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.
When Methuselah was 187 years old, he became the father of Lamech.
And after he had become the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.
When Lamech was 182 years old, he had a son.
And he named him Noah, saying,
May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed.
And after he had become the father of Noah, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.
After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

Evening in {OUTSIDE}: {ADAM_SKIN}, and {EVE_SKIN}, seated close together beside a small fire in front of {SHELTER}, he drawing a hide gently around her shoulders, she leaning her head against him. Both fully clothed. {TWO}. Medium view.

The first child ever born: {EVE_SKIN}, seated inside {SHELTER} in soft morning light, cradling {INFANT} with thick black hair against her shoulder, weary and full of wonder. Exactly one woman and one baby, no one else. Medium close view.

{EVE_SKIN}, standing outside at sunrise and holding {INFANT} up before her in both hands, her face lifted to the bright sky with joy, speaking; beside her {ADAM_SKIN}, looks at the child. Exactly one man, one woman and one baby. Medium view.

{EVE_SKIN}, seated on the ground holding {INFANT} in her arms, while a sturdy little boy of about three with thick black hair, dressed in a small skin garment, leans on her knee and looks down at his baby brother. Exactly one woman, one small boy and one baby. Medium view.

A keeper of sheep: {ABEL}, walking across a grassy hillside in morning light at the head of a flock of sheep, a plain wooden staff in one hand and a small lamb carried in the crook of his other arm. {ONE}. Wide view.
A tiller of the soil: {CAIN}, bent over in {FIELD}, driving a stout pointed wooden digging stick into the hard earth with both hands, sweat on his brow. {ONE}. Medium view.
{CAIN}, climbing a bare hillside toward {STONES} at the top, carrying sheaves of grain under one arm and a gourd and bunches of grapes in the other. {ONE}. Wide view.
An offering of the fruit of the soil: close view of a man's strong brown hands setting down {PRODUCE}, on top of {STONES}. Only the hands and forearms are in the frame; no face. Close view.
The firstborn of his flock: {ABEL}, kneeling among his sheep and gently lifting the finest young lamb out from the flock in both arms. {ONE}. Medium view.
{ABEL}, kneeling with bowed head before {STONES} on a green hilltop, laying upon it with both hands his offering, wrapped in a clean white fleece. {NOGORE}. {ONE}. Medium view.

{ABEL}, kneeling beside {STONES} that bears his offering wrapped in a white fleece, lifting his face with quiet joy as {GLORY}, rests warm on him and on his offering. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium-wide view.

{CAIN}, standing stiffly before {STONES} that bears {PRODUCE}, under a flat grey sky; no light falls on him or on his offering, while far away in the background a single shaft of golden light falls on another distant hilltop. {ONE}. Wide view.
Close view of the face of {CAIN}, very angry, jaw clenched, brows drawn down, his eyes cast to the ground, his face in grey shadow. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

Seen over the shoulder of {CAIN}, in dark foreground shadow with his fist clenched at his side: he glares across a shallow valley at {ABEL}, small in the distance, kneeling in a pool of golden light on the far hilltop. {TWOMEN}. Wide view from behind Cain.

{CAIN}, alone in {FIELD}, at dusk, standing with his head down and his arms hanging, while {GLORY}, opens above him and lights the furrows around his feet; he does not look up. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view.

Close view of the face of {CAIN}, one side lit by warm golden light from above, the other in deep shadow, his eyes lifting half-way toward the light, torn and unwilling. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

Sin is crouching at the door: night, the dark open doorway of {SHELTER}, and close beside the doorway on the ground a dense shapeless black shadow, low and hunched like a beast about to spring, with no eyes, no face and no clear form. {NOPEOPLE}. Low medium view.

{CAIN}, standing in the doorway of {SHELTER}, at night with both fists clenched, looking down at a shapeless black shadow that lies low across the threshold at his feet; behind him, far off, a last line of golden light fades from the sky. {ONE}. Medium view.

{CAIN}, on the left, his hand on the shoulder of {ABEL}, on the right, and pointing with his other arm out toward open fields; Abel turns to him with a trusting look, a plain wooden staff in his hand. {TWOMEN}. Medium view.

Two brothers alone in a wide empty field of tall grain under a heavy sky, far from any dwelling: {ABEL}, walking ahead with his staff, and {CAIN}, two steps behind him, staring at his brother's back. {TWOMEN}. Wide view.

Cain rises up against his brother: {CAIN}, seen from a low angle against a dark stormy sky, lunging forward with his face twisted in fury and both empty clenched fists raised high above his head. He holds no weapon. {ONE}. The brother is not in the picture. {NOGORE}. Low-angle medium view.

The field afterward, in silence: a plain wooden shepherd's staff lies in trampled grain in the foreground, and beyond it a slender man in a pale sheepskin garment lies motionless on the ground, turned away from the viewer and half hidden by the standing grain. {NOGORE}. Exactly one figure, lying still, his face not seen. Low wide view.
{CAIN}, hurrying away across an empty field, stopped in mid-stride as {GLORY}, breaks through dark clouds directly in front of him and blocks his way. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view from the side.
Close view of {CAIN}, chin thrust up, looking sideways into strong golden light with a hard, defiant face, his mouth open in a sharp answer and one empty hand flung out. Head and chest only. {ONE}.
{CAIN}, staggering a step backward with one arm thrown up to shield his eyes as {GLORY}, blazes suddenly brighter over the field in front of him. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium-wide view.

The blood cries out from the ground: close view at ground level of trampled earth between broken stalks of grain, the soil darkened by a deep red stain that is soaking into the ground, a shaft of golden light falling directly on it. No body and no person in the frame. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view at ground level.

The ground has opened its mouth: a long dark crack splitting open across dry bare soil in the middle of a field of withering grain, the earth at its edges stained dark red. {NOPEOPLE}. High close view looking down.
{CAIN}, staring down in horror at his own two open hands held out in front of him, the palms darkened with earth, golden light glaring on them. {ONE}. Medium close view.
{CAIN}, on his knees clawing with a digging stick at ground that has turned dry, grey and cracked, the rows of grain around him withered and brown, dust blowing. {ONE}. Medium view.

A fugitive and a wanderer on the earth: one tiny lone figure of a man walking away across a vast empty wasteland of stone and dust under an enormous sky, with no path, no shelter and no other living thing. Exactly one tiny figure. Very wide view.
{CAIN}, fallen to his knees on the bare ground with both arms spread wide, his face lifted in anguish into {GLORY}. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium-wide view.
Close view of the face of {CAIN}, pleading, tears on his cheeks, as the golden light on his face fades and a cold blue shadow covers it from one side. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

{CAIN}, seen from behind, kneeling at the edge of the tilled land and looking out over a dark, endless wilderness of rock and thorn that lies ahead of him, a golden light behind the viewer throwing his long shadow out toward it. {ONE}. Wide view from behind.

Whoever finds me will kill me: {CAIN}, at night in a narrow rocky gully, pressed against a rock and looking back over his shoulder in fear at the empty darkness behind him. {ONE}. No pursuer is seen. Medium view.
{CAIN}, kneeling with his head bowed to the ground, while {GLORY}, flares out strongly all around him on every side like a wall of light. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view.

The LORD places a mark on Cain: {CAIN}, seen from behind and slightly above, kneeling with his head bowed low, as one narrow ray of golden-white light comes down and rests on his bowed head and shoulders. He is seen from behind: his face and brow are not visible. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium view from behind.

{CAIN}, seen from behind, rising slowly to his feet alone on the bare ground, his head still lowered, the golden light withdrawing upward into the clouds above him. Seen from behind: his face is not visible. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view from behind.

Cain goes out from the presence of the LORD: {CAIN}, seen from behind, walking away into a dim grey land, with a great golden light behind the viewer throwing his long shadow far out ahead of him. Seen from behind: his face is not visible. {ONE}. Wide view from behind.

The land of Nod, east of Eden: a harsh dry upland of red rock and scattered thorn trees at dusk, where one small lone man in a dark skin garment crouches over a small fire he has kindled in the shelter of a boulder. Exactly one small figure. Very wide view.

Outside a hut of rough stones and branches in a dry upland: {CAIN}, seen from behind, seated on the ground beside {CAINWIFE}, who faces the viewer holding {INFANT} in her arms and looking down at the child. Cain is seen from behind: his face is not visible. Exactly one man, one woman and one baby. Medium view.

Cain builds a city: {CAIN}, seen from behind, heaving a heavy rough stone up onto a half-built wall of stones and mud brick, while a small boy of about six in a skin garment stands beside him carrying a smaller stone in both arms. Cain is seen from behind: his face is not visible. Exactly one man and one boy. Medium view.
The city called Enoch: {CITY}, seen at evening with thin smoke rising from cooking fires and tiny figures of people and goats moving at the open gateway. Very wide view.

Generation after generation: in the doorway of a mud-brick house, four generations of one family of men in dark wool tunics: a white-bearded great-grandfather seated, a grey-bearded grandfather standing, a young father, and in the young father's arms a newborn baby that he is holding out to the grandfather. Exactly three men and one baby. Medium view.

Many years later: {CITY}, now grown much larger, with new houses spilling beyond the old wall, tilled plots, herds grazing on the plain and many tiny figures on the tracks leading to it, in hard noon light. Very wide high view.

{LAMECH_C}, standing in front of a mud-brick house between his two wives, one heavy hand resting on the shoulder of each: on the left {ADAH}, and on the right {ZILLAH}. {THREE}. Medium view, full figures.

Jabal, father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock: a young herdsman in a rough wool tunic with a wooden staff, driving cattle, goats and sheep across a grassy plain past a camp of low dark goat-hair tents. Exactly one herdsman in the foreground. Wide view.

Tent dwellers at work: two men and a woman in rough wool tunics raising a low tent of dark goat-hair cloth on wooden poles, hauling its ropes taut and driving in a wooden peg with a stone, while goats graze behind them. Medium view.

Jubal, father of all who play the harp and flute: a young man in a rough wool tunic seated on a rock by a camp fire at evening, eyes half closed, playing a small hand-held wooden harp with a few gut strings; beside him a boy plays a simple reed flute, and a few listeners sit in the shadows. Medium view.

Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron: a muscular young smith with a leather apron over a wool tunic, hammering a glowing blade on a flat stone anvil beside a small clay furnace full of red coals, sparks flying in the dark workshop. Exactly one person. Medium view.

Implements of bronze and iron: close view of a rough stone bench beside glowing coals, on which lie newly made tools: a bronze axe head, a bronze sickle, a bronze knife, a dark iron hoe blade and a dark iron chisel; a smith's hand sets down one more tool. Only the hand is in the frame; no face. Close view.

Naamah, the sister of Tubal-cain: a young woman with long black hair in a rough dark wool dress standing at the entrance of the forge, firelight on her face, watching; behind her, deep in the workshop, the young smith in a leather apron bends over his furnace. Exactly two people. Medium view.

Night, inside a mud-brick house lit by a fire: {LAMECH_C}, striding in through the doorway with both arms spread wide, shouting; on the left {ADAH}, and on the right {ZILLAH}, turn toward him, startled. {THREE}. Medium-wide view.

Close view of {LAMECH_C}, boasting in firelight, striking his own chest with his fist and grinning fiercely; his upper arm is tightly bound with a strip of wool cloth over a wound. Head and chest only. {ONE}. {NOGORE}.

A young man slain: dusk on a stony track outside the wall of a mud-brick city, where a young man in a wool tunic lies motionless on the ground in the middle distance, turned away from the viewer, a wooden club dropped beside him. {NOGORE}. Exactly one figure, lying still, his face not seen. Wide view.

{LAMECH_C}, seen from a low angle in firelight, thrusting his clenched fist high into the air and roaring his boast, while behind him in the shadows {ADAH}, and {ZILLAH}, draw back close together. {THREE}. Low-angle medium view.

{ADAM_SKIN}, and {EVE_SKIN}, standing close together at dusk beside {GRAVE}, at the edge of a field, his arm around her shoulders, both looking down at it in grief. Both fully clothed. {TWO}. Medium-wide view.

{EVE_SKIN}, seated at the entrance of {SHELTER}, in gentle morning light, holding {INFANT} with dark curly hair close against her cheek, her eyes closed. Exactly one woman and one baby, no one else. Medium close view.

{EVE_SKIN}, holding {INFANT} in her arms and looking upward, speaking, tears and thankfulness together on her face; beside her {ADAM_SKIN}, looks down at the child. Behind them a plain wooden shepherd's staff leans unused against {SHELTER}. Exactly one man, one woman and one baby. Medium view.
{SETH}, standing in a field in bright morning light, holding {INFANT} up in both hands in front of him and smiling at the child. Exactly one man and one baby. Medium view.
{SETH}, standing on a hilltop at dawn with both hands lifted and his face turned up to the sky in prayer, while behind him men, women and children of his family kneel on the grass. Medium view.

Men begin to call upon the name of the LORD: a great gathering of men, women and children in skins and rough wool standing on a wide hilltop at sunrise, all with their hands lifted to the sky, golden light breaking over them from the clouds. {NOLIGHTFIG}. No altar, no idol and no building. Very wide view.

The generations of Adam: a long line of men walking one behind another along the crest of a ridge at dawn, each a father followed by his son, dark silhouettes against a glowing sky, the line stretching away into the far distance. Very wide view.

The day God created man: in a lush sunlit garden, the small dark silhouette of one man standing waist-deep in tall ferns and grasses with his face lifted into {GLORY}. He is a plain dark silhouette with no detail of his body visible. Exactly one small figure. Wide view.

Male and female He created them: in a lush sunlit garden, the two small dark silhouettes of a man and a woman standing side by side, hand in hand, waist-deep in ferns and flowers under {GLORY}. They are plain dark silhouettes with no detail of their bodies visible. Exactly two small figures. Wide view.
{ADAM_SKIN}, holding {INFANT} with dark curly hair like his own up close in front of his face and studying the child's features with wonder. Exactly one man and one baby. Medium close view.

A son in his own likeness: years later, a father and his grown son who look strikingly alike, standing side by side in the same pose, each leaning on a wooden digging stick at the edge of a field: on the left {ADAM_SKIN}, and on the right {SETH}. {TWOMEN}. Medium view.

Adam in great old age among his other sons and daughters: seen from behind, a very old man with white curly hair in a garment of tawny animal skin sits on a rock, and gathered on the ground in front of him, facing the viewer, are many sons, daughters and grandchildren of every age, listening to him. The old man is seen only from behind. Wide view.

The death of Adam: {GRAVE}, newly raised beneath a great old tree at dusk, and around it a large crowd of mourners of every age in skins and rough wool, all seen from behind with bowed heads. Wide view from behind the mourners.
Dust to dust: close view at ground level of dry dust blowing in the evening wind across the base of {GRAVE}. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view at ground level.
{SETH}, walking through a field of ripe grain with a laughing little boy of about three riding on his shoulders. Exactly one man and one small boy. Medium view.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 4:1–5:32, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 4:1-26 and 5:1-32 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, E Eve, C Cain, G the voice of God, L Lamech of Cain's line (4:23-24), M Lamech the father of Noah (5:29). Abel never speaks in the text and has no voice.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip). Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces: ADAM_SKIN and EVE_SKIN reuse refs/REF-ADAM-SKIN.jpg and refs/REF-EVE-SKIN.jpg and the description text from s01e01c word for word. New sheets made by this unit: refs/REF-CAIN.jpg, REF-ABEL.jpg, REF-LAMECH-CAIN.jpg, REF-SETH.jpg, REF-ENOCH.jpg (Enoch of Seth's line, 5:21-24) and REF-NOAH.jpg. Later units must reuse the NOAH description text unchanged.

Two men are named Enoch and two Lamech. Cain's son Enoch (4:17) appears only as a baby and a boy; ENOCH is the man who walked with God. LAMECH_C (shaved head, scar, wolf pelt) is Cain's descendant; LAMECH_N (block) is Noah's father and is described so that the two cannot be confused.

Ages: the text gives ages of 65 to 187 at fatherhood and lifespans up to 969. Fathers are painted as men in their prime at the birth of the named son and as white-haired in the long years after (I). Adam at 130 (4:25, 5:3) keeps the face of his sheet; his great age (5:4) is shown only from behind. Noah at 500 is painted as a weathered man of about fifty (I); his three sons are small boys in 5:32 and are not told apart, since their birth order is disputed.
4:1, 4:17, 4:25 ('had relations'): implied only, the couple shown clothed and together, then the child (PIPELINE default).

The offerings (4:3-5): the text names no altar and no fire and does not say how favor was shown. Each offering is laid on a heap of field stones (I) with no fire; favor is golden light resting on Abel and his offering, and no light on Cain's (D). 'The best portions of the firstborn' are shown as a firstborn lamb chosen (C3) and an offering wrapped in fleece (C4), with no slaughter shown.
4:7: 'sin is crouching at your door' is pictured as a shapeless shadow at the door of Cain's shelter (D). God speaks as light only, never a figure.

The killing (4:8): the text names no weapon and no manner, so Cain's hands are empty (F3) and the blow is not shown; Abel is seen afterward lying still, face unseen, without wound or blood (F4). 4:10-11: a red stain soaking into the soil and a crack in the ground stand for the blood crying out and the ground opening its mouth; no body in those frames.

The mark on Cain (4:15): the text does not say what it was and the question is disputed, so it is not resolved: a ray of light rests on Cain seen from behind, and from that verse on Cain is only shown from behind or as a tiny distant figure, so that no mark is ever pictured.

Cain's wife (4:17) is unnamed and where she came from is not explained by the text; she is simply shown. The city of Enoch is a small walled cluster of mud-brick and stone houses (I). O1 and O2 picture the passing generations of 4:18 (D).

4:19-22: Adah, Zillah, Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain and Naamah have description text only (ADAH, ZILLAH blocks; the others appear once). The 'harp' is a small hand-held wooden harp and the 'flute' a reed flute (I). 4:23: Lamech's wound is a bound arm (T: 'for wounding me'); the slain young man lies distant, face unseen, no blood (S3).
T1 (Adam and Eve at a grave before Seth's birth) and the staff in T3 are D: the text does not describe Abel's burial.

Genesis 5: the refrain 'and then he died' is pictured each time without a face: a grave of stones, a bier, a still hand, a staff by a grave, an empty place at a fire. The graves and mourning customs are I. V1 the line of fathers and sons is D. V2-V3 recall the creation of 1:27 with distant silhouettes only.

Enoch (5:21-24): 'walked with God' is a radiance moving beside him on the path, no figure (WALKLIGHT). 'He was no more, because God had taken him away' is shown as the text says it and not explained: he walks toward the light (EH5), then footprints that end on an empty path (EH6). EH7, his family looking up the path, is D.
ME3 (Methuselah's grave under gathering rain clouds) and NO2 (cloud on the horizon) are D and look ahead to Genesis 6-7; the text itself draws no connection.
Voices for Cain and the two Lamechs are placeholders chosen without hearing them (God and Eve as in s01e01a-c); narration is not generated in this unit.
